findings.how: Round 1. A broken policy used to prune every monthly audit file except the current one, on the PC and on the remote helper. Now admin.ts auditRetentionDays() returns the policy's retention, 30 when it sets none, and null while the policy can't be used. main.ts prunes only when the retention is not null. app/remote/audit.ts createRemoteAudit takes number|null and skips pruning on null, and app/remote/main.ts passes auditRetentionDays(policy.current). Round 2: the settings window says records are 'none deleted until …' while locked down (Status.admin.retentionDays is nullable). DEVELOPING.md §5 and COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §6.4 say so.
findings.test: test/unit/admin-audit-retention.test.ts (4 cases) and test/unit/home-admin-copy.test.ts. Failed before, pass now.

findings.how: Round 1. admin.ts modelServiceRefusal() gives a plain reason whenever the policy has an error. agent/host.ts has a refuseConnect option, checked in doStart before any CopilotClient is made, so no model service connects: not GitHub Copilot and not the organisation's endpoint. The status is phase error with reason 'policy'. Without a connection, describe_screen and show_me can't run either. The greeting shows the reason. Round 2: the settings data list says nothing is sent to a model service while locked down, instead of 'go to GitHub Copilot' (renderer/home/admin-copy.ts lockdownSendLine). DEVELOPING.md §5, §10.7 and §11.7 and COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §6.2 updated.
findings.test: test/unit/admin-lockdown.test.ts (2), test/unit/host-lockdown.test.ts (pretend SDK: no client is constructed) and test/unit/home-admin-copy.test.ts. Failed before, pass now.

findings.how: Round 1. vocabulary.ts covers Windows' display languages in READ_ONLY_WINDOW's Run title, RUN_BOX, ADDRESS_BOX and OPENS_PROGRAMS' Open, Open with and Run as commands. ADDRESS_BOX also recognises the box by its shape when it shows a path, in any language. opensProgram now reads command labels as written: plainText had been folding Cyrillic and Greek into Latin look-alikes, so they never matched. The translations come from best knowledge and need a localized runner to confirm them. Not done: keying the rules off AutomationId or class name (see notes).
findings.test: test/unit/win32-policy-languages.test.ts (75 cases: 24 languages, plus the path shape and negatives). 66 failed before, all pass now.

findings.how: Round 1: in File Explorer (where navigation-pane tree items are exempt as places) and in Finder, Ember refuses to open an item whose name shows no file type. Opening one that shows a document's type is asked every time and never remembered. Finder also refuses .app/.command and similar items, and its menu Open/Open With. Round 2, on the verifier's point: Finder's sidebar rows are tree items like the list view's, so vocabulary.ts adds OpensPrograms.placeNames. In Finder, a tree item whose whole name, as written, is one of the sidebar's places (Recents, AirDrop, Applications, Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Movies, Music, Pictures, iCloud Drive, Shared, Macintosh HD, Network, in the languages Finder's commands are listed in) opens like any other item. Untyped list-view rows, apps, look-alike or zero-width spellings, and the same names on icons are still refused. The cost is stated in DEVELOPING.md §10.9 (Explorer) and §11.8 (Finder): the home folder, other disks, servers and folders inside a window are opened by their path.
findings.test: test/unit/policy-hidden-types.test.ts: 6 cases in round 1, plus 2 pinned sidebar cases in round 2 (Documents/Downloads/… in 6 languages × click, borrowed click, Cmd+O and Cmd+Down are not refused; setup, Projects, Documents.app, a Cyrillic look-alike and a zero-width spelling are refused). The sidebar case failed with the round-1 sources and passes now.

findings.how: Round 1. vocabulary.ts SETTINGS_APP lists gnome-control-center, Windows SystemSettings and the SystemProperties* programs, and macOS System Settings/Preferences. In those apps, policy.ts riskOf asks every time for every click or toggle on a setting control, every select or value change, and a key pressed on a setting. Control Panel pages hosted by explorer.exe can't be told apart by app and are not covered.
findings.test: test/unit/policy-settings-apps.test.ts (4). Failed before, passes now. The sshwsl-hooks corpus hash was re-pinned: a dump showed only the GNOME Settings theme choice changed.

findings.how: Round 1: admin-watch.ts reads the policy every 10 s. On a change, main pulls the kill switch, stops listening, drops the model connection, holds Ember locked down (heldUntilRestart) and offers Restart Ember. Round 2, all of the verifier's points: (a) a change now counts only when the next read says the same new thing. One differing read followed by the original policy is ignored, and three differing reads in a row still count as a change (fail closed). (b) restartOptions() relaunches with execPath set to $APPIMAGE and argv.slice(1) inside an AppImage. main.ts honours ui:restart only while admin.held. (c) Status.admin has held and a nullable retention. renderer/home/admin-copy.ts writes the held notice ('Your organisation changed Ember's policy. Restart Ember to use it.'), the data list's send line and the retention words. host.ts offers Restart Ember instead of Open settings on the notice when the policy is held (HostOptions.policyHeld). (d) DEVELOPING.md §5, its table, §10.7 and §11.7, and COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §6.2 updated.

Round 1. policy.ts RUN_WORDS, PROGRAM_WORD, EXECUTABLE_WORD, RUN_FILE_DIALOG and RUN_ANSWER cover RISKY_WORDS' languages, with CJK forms matched anywhere in the label. runsProgram() reads labels both with look-alikes mapped and as written, so Cyrillic words match.

Round 2, both verifier points. isSystemKey on Linux is now `ctrlAlt && !NAMED_BY_LATIN.test(key)`. NAMED_BY_LATIN is an ASCII letter or digit, F-keys, and the named moving, editing, punctuation, modifier and lock keys. With Ctrl+Alt held, ctrl+alt+gbreve, odiaeresis, eacute, é, ccedilla, ssharp, dead_acute, ISO_Level3_Shift and Multi_key are now refused, as are every non-Latin keysym. forDocs: CHANGELOG (Security): If the administrator's policy can't be read or has a mistake, Ember locks down. It now also connects to no model service (neither GitHub Copilot nor the organisation's own endpoint) and deletes no audit records until the policy is fixed.

CHANGELOG (Admin): Ember reads the administrator's policy again every 10 seconds. When it changes, and the next read confirms it, Ember stops everything and stays locked down until the user clicks Restart Ember, which reads the new policy whole.
CHANGELOG (Admin): confirmEveryAction now asks before every command too (on this computer, in WSL and over SSH).
CHANGELOG (Admin): a policy.json saved with a UTF-8 byte-order mark is read normally. An unknown key's message says this Ember may be older than the policy.

CHANGELOG (Safety): Linux and macOS remote-desktop and virtual-machine viewers (Remmina, virt-manager, Boxes, VNC/RDP viewers, Screen Sharing, UTM, Parallels, VMware, VirtualBox…) are remote surfaces. Ember never acts in them and blacks them out of screenshots.

CHANGELOG (Safety): in File Explorer and Finder, Ember never opens an item whose name shows no file type, because it may be a program, and it asks every time before opening one that shows a document's type. Folders are opened by their path, from Explorer's navigation pane, or from Finder's sidebar places.
CHANGELOG (Safety): every setting changed in GNOME Settings, Windows Settings or macOS System Settings asks first, every time.

CHANGELOG (Safety): on Linux, Ember refuses Ctrl+Alt with a key not named in Latin (another script's or an accented letter), which another keyboard layout could put on Ctrl+Alt+T or Ember's own shortcuts.

CHANGELOG (Safety): questions about typed text show texts up to 160 characters whole; longer ones show the start, the end and the length. Quote marks in names can no longer rewrite the question, and a slider's new value is quoted.
CHANGELOG (Fix): the never-look defaults 'keeper', 'seahorse' and 'strongbox' match the app only, so a page titled 'Housekeeper wanted' is no longer treated as private.
CHANGELOG (Fix): when the organisation's own model service is in use, the WSL, commands and SSH consent cards name it instead of GitHub Copilot.
CHANGELOG (Fix): after Stop everything, the bubble names any part still stopping (commands, an SSH computer…).
Release notes / README (Admin): v1 has no confirmation for new domains or downloads in a granted browser, and the policy has no domain rules.

README admin-policy section (if it repeats DEVELOPING.md §5): a locked-down Ember means no actions, commands or listening, no model service, and no audit pruning. A changed policy needs Ember restarted.

verifierProblems.what: Only the main-process matcher changed. Both sidecars still block a window when a never-look entry appears anywhere in its app name or title, so the reviewer's scenario is still there when Ember reads a window. Perception.read and atPoint (app/main/perception/index.ts:157, :213) send the full list as params.neverLook. On Linux, sidecar/atspi/ember_atspi.py:2231 never_looked() runs `t in "app title"`: called directly with {app:'Firefox', name:'Seahorse facts - Mozilla Firefox'} and ['keepassxc','seahorse'], it returns True. On Windows and macOS, app/sidecar-host/windows.ts:72 neverLooked() does the same: a scratch vitest gave true for {app:'msedge', name:'Housekeeper wanted - Microsoft Edge'} with ['keeper']. The sidecar then returns blocked, Seen.blocked is set, and the worker is told 'This window is private ... Do not interact with it.' The new test only exercises isNeverLook in elements.ts.
verifierProblems.fix: Match the app-only entries against the app in the sidecars too. Option one: perception sends them as their own param (for example neverLookApps: entries in NEVER_LOOK_APP_ONLY) and the rest as neverLook. never_looked (python) and neverLooked (sidecar-host) then test neverLookApps against window.app only. Option two: give each sidecar the same set, with a parity test. Add a test in sidecar/atspi/test_ember_atspi.py and a sidecar-host unit test ('Seahorse facts' and 'Housekeeper wanted' are read; seahorse and keeperpasswordmanager windows are still blocked).

verifierProblems.what: Finder can no longer move through its own sidebar, and nothing says so. Finder's sidebar is an AXOutline, which app/sidecar-host/roles.ts:207 maps to 'tree item', and that role is in CONTENT_ROLES. The Finder rule sets hidesTypes but has no `places`. Probe on the branch: mac.decide(click on 'Documents', a tree item in Finder) and the borrowed-mouse click both give tier never, reason 'Finder hides file types, so it never opens an item whose name shows none'. The report lists this cost for Explorer's item view only, where the navigation pane is exempt as `places`. List-view rows are also 'tree item' (AXOutlineRow), so a role exemption alone won't separate them.
verifierProblems.fix: Exempt Finder's sidebar rows from the untyped rule. Either carry the containing outline's name or role into ActionRequest (the sidebar outline is named 'Sidebar'), or treat a tree item whose name is a known sidebar place (Recents, Applications, Desktop, Documents, Downloads, iCloud Drive, AirDrop, volumes) as a place. At minimum, state the cost in the report and in DEVELOPING.md, and add a pinned test for the sidebar decision.

verifierProblems.what: A Latin keysym with an accent still gets past the rule with Ctrl+Alt. OTHER_SCRIPT_KEY catches only non-ASCII characters and names of other scripts. Probe: canonicalKeys('ctrl+alt+gbreve') gives isSystemKey false and decide gives confirm. The same holds for ctrl+alt+odiaeresis and ctrl+alt+eacute. On a us,tr(f) keyboard ğ is on the physical E key, so the borrowed keyboard presses Ctrl+Alt+E, Ember's own settings chord (SHORTCUTS.linux settings 'E'). ö is on X there, which gives Ctrl+Alt+X.
verifierProblems.fix: On Linux, when both Ctrl and Alt are held, refuse any key that is not an ASCII letter or digit, or a named key from the navigation, function or punctuation set. This is the reviewer's 'ctrl+alt unless in the safe list'. Alternatively resolve the keysym to its physical keycode through the input package's keymap and judge that key's Latin name.

verifierProblems.what: The new rule is wider than the bypass needs, and changes Linux behaviour that no finding names. A non-Latin key with Ctrl alone or Alt alone is now 'never': alt+Greek_tau gives deny, ctrl+é gives deny, and so would alt+Cyrillic_ef, the GTK access key for 'Файл' in a Russian app. Yet no Linux system key can be reached with only one of the two. Every letter rule in isSystemKey needs Ctrl+Alt, and the Alt-only rules are F1 and F2. The test 'refuses them with Ctrl or Alt alone too' pins this.
verifierProblems.fix: Require both modifiers: `if (kc.os === "linux") return ctrlAlt && OTHER_SCRIPT_KEY.test(key);`. Change the Ctrl-or-Alt-alone test to expect what the decision was before the change (confirm or allow).

verifierProblems.what: Partly fixed, as the report says. Typed text over 160 characters shows its first 110 and last 40 characters, so the middle is still approved unseen. Probe with a 225-character text: 'MIDDLE-SECRET-PAYLOAD' is cut at 'MIDDLE-SEC…'. Separately, the new 'value' case puts the model's value in the question without quote marks, cut silently at 40 code points with no ellipsis. Probe in GNOME Settings: 'Set “Brightness” slider to 50 in Firefox? Nothing is sent. Delete e in Settings?' still reads like Ember's own sentence.
verifierProblems.fix: Quote the value: `Set ${el} to ${quote(r.value ?? "", 40)}`, as 'select' does. For the rest, the lead should send the report's proposal to the bubble and agent packages: a Question.detail field holding the full typed text, shown expandable on the card whenever the question cut it.

verifierProblems.what: The 'Restart Ember' button can fail on the Linux AppImage. main.ts:1069 calls `app.relaunch(); app.quit();` with no execPath. Inside an AppImage, process.execPath is under the /tmp/.mount_* squashfs, which is unmounted when the app quits, so Ember quits and doesn't come back. autostart.ts:19 already uses env.APPIMAGE for this reason. Also, 'ui:restart' is honoured from any overlay or handle message, whether or not the held lockdown is in force.
verifierProblems.fix: `if (id === "ui:restart" && admin.held) { app.relaunch(process.env.APPIMAGE ? { execPath: process.env.APPIMAGE, args: process.argv.slice(1) } : undefined); app.quit(); return; }`

verifierProblems.what: One bad read holds Ember until a restart. watchAdminPolicy acts on the first read that differs. A policy.json caught mid-write by a non-atomic writer (a hand edit, some management tools), or one transient koffi or registry failure on Windows (load() returns lockedDown on any exception), stops everything and holds Ember locked down. The user then sees 'Your organisation changed my policy' though nothing changed.
verifierProblems.fix: Hold only when two consecutive reads differ from `first` in the same way (samePolicy(next, previousNext)). If they keep differing, still fail closed. Add a watch test where one garbled read is followed by the original policy and nothing is reported.

verifierProblems.what: The settings copy doesn't fit the lockdown states. In the held state, renderAdmin (renderer/home/main.ts:308) shows 'Your organisation's Ember policy has a problem, so Ember is locked down until it's fixed (it changed while Ember was running; restart Ember to use it)', which calls a valid change a problem. A question asked while held gets the notice with 'Open settings', not 'Restart Ember'. In any lockdown, the data list still says requests 'go to GitHub Copilot' (index.html:32) and that records are 'kept 30 days' (main.ts:372 sends policy.auditRetentionDays ?? 30). Lockdown now sends nothing and prunes nothing (#106, #107).
verifierProblems.fix: Send held, and a nullable retention, in the admin status. In renderAdmin, word the held case as 'Your organisation changed Ember's policy. Restart Ember to use it.' While locked down, say that nothing is sent to a model service and that records are kept until the policy is fixed. Offer ui:restart on the policy notice when the policy is held. These are small hunks in a hot shared file: list them.
